dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Existing official HD-EPIC research recording; retain source attribution.

observed_events.description: A black broad round-headed cooking tool contacts rice-like contents inside a deep round straight-sided saucepan. The wearer holds its single long wooden-look handle. No retail model, capacity or material is inferred.

A metal spoon rests in a different shiny saucepan soaking in the sink, beside a metal ladle. The wearer picks the spoon up from this black-handled saucepan. This is an actual resting-in relation, not a fabricated cooking-use claim.

The wearer holds the round-headed cooking tool in one hand while taking a plate from the upper cupboard. Neither the earlier rice saucepan nor the lifted dishwasher pan is visible in these final two images.

unsupported_claims: The source confirms an exact retail material, size or model
A utensil resting in the sink saucepan proves it was used there for cooking
A wood-look handle establishes actual wood material

screening.real_user_need: I like the look of the handle on the pan I handled here. Add a spare to my cart, matching its general body shape and handle appearance. Brand, size and material can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid or other accessories are fine.
screening.scope_note: New cookware-to-utensil relation. Existing knife-order tasks and model trials remain unchanged.
screening.proposed_instruction: I like the look of the handle on the pan I handled here. Add a spare to my cart, matching its general body shape and handle appearance. Brand, size and material can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid or other accessories are fine.

construct.research_question: Can a later isolated utensil cue retrieve its earlier cookware binding, with that binding naturally farther back or nearer?
construct.belief_before: The brown wood-look-handled rice saucepan and black-handled soaking saucepan each have a different utensil-in-pan relation.
construct.belief_after: The isolated utensil held at the cupboard links to the earlier deep rice saucepan.
construct.required_behavior_change: Link the isolated final wooden tool to its earlier cookware partner, then buy one corresponding pan.
construct.no_update_failure: Without the physical clarification both pans remain plausible.
construct.overupdate_failure: Choosing a utensil instead of cookware, or buying both cookware branches, fails the one-pan request.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The end frame gives the tool but not either pan; the earlier relation gives the associated saucepan's shape. The reply itself gives no colour, tool-head class or cookware shape.

task_blueprint.ambiguous_instruction: I like the look of the handle on the pan I handled here. Add a spare to my cart, matching its general body shape and handle appearance. Brand, size and material can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid or other accessories are fine.
task_blueprint.oracle_instruction: I like the look of the handle on the pan that the utensil I am holding at the upper cupboard at the end was in earlier. Add a spare to my cart, matching its general body shape and handle appearance. Brand, size and material can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid or other accessories are fine.
task_blueprint.canonical_answer: The pan that the utensil I am holding at the upper cupboard at the end was in earlier.

supported_claims.text: A black broad round-headed cooking tool contacts rice-like contents inside a deep round straight-sided saucepan. The wearer holds its single long wooden-look handle. No retail model, capacity or material is inferred.

A metal spoon rests in a different shiny saucepan soaking in the sink, beside a metal ladle. The wearer picks the spoon up from this black-handled saucepan. This is an actual resting-in relation, not a fabricated cooking-use claim.

The wearer holds the round-headed cooking tool in one hand while taking a plate from the upper cupboard. Neither the earlier rice saucepan nor the lifted dishwasher pan is visible in these final two images.

screening.real_user_need: I like the look of the handle on the pan I handled here. Add a spare to my cart, matching its general body shape and handle appearance. Brand, size and material can differ. One pan, not a multi-pan set; a lid or other accessories are fine.

construct.research_question: Can a later isolated utensil cue retrieve its earlier cookware binding, with that binding naturally farther back or nearer?
construct.belief_before: The brown wood-look-handled rice saucepan and black-handled soaking saucepan each have a different utensil-in-pan relation.
construct.belief_after: The isolated utensil held at the cupboard links to the earlier deep rice saucepan.
construct.required_behavior_change: Link the isolated final wooden tool to its earlier cookware partner, then buy one corresponding pan.
construct.no_update_failure: Without the physical clarification both pans remain plausible.
construct.overupdate_failure: Choosing a utensil instead of cookware, or buying both cookware branches, fails the one-pan request.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The end frame gives the tool but not either pan; the earlier relation gives the associated saucepan's shape. The reply itself gives no colour, tool-head class or cookware shape.

supported_claims.text: A black broad round-headed cooking tool contacts rice-like contents inside a deep round straight-sided saucepan. The wearer holds its single long wooden-look handle. No retail model, capacity or material is inferred.

A metal spoon rests in a different shiny saucepan soaking in the sink, beside a metal ladle. The wearer picks the spoon up from this black-handled saucepan. This is an actual resting-in relation, not a fabricated cooking-use claim.

The wearer holds the round-headed cooking tool in one hand while taking a plate from the upper cupboard. Neither the earlier rice saucepan nor the lifted dishwasher pan is visible in these final two images.
